questions.text:
(a) (4 marks) State with reasons whether the following statements are True or False:
(i) Provision for discount on debtors is created on gross debtors before deducting provision for doubtful debts.
(ii) A change in the method of depreciation from SLM to WDV is a change in accounting policy.
(iii) Goods sent on approval basis are treated as sales at the time of despatch.
(iv) Under the Sales of Goods Act principle followed in consignment, the consignee is the owner of goods.

(b) (4 marks) The Trial Balance of Rohit as on 31.3.2026 did not agree; the difference of Rs. 2,150 (excess credit) was placed in a Suspense Account. Later the following errors were found:
(i) Purchase Day Book undercast by Rs. 1,000.
(ii) Rs. 4,500 received from Mohan credited to Sohan.
(iii) Sales Return Book overcast by Rs. 800.
(iv) Rs. 3,150 paid for machinery repairs debited to Machinery A/c.
(v) Discount allowed Rs. 350 posted to the debit of Discount Received A/c.
Pass rectifying journal entries and prepare the Suspense Account.

(c) (6 marks) On 1.4.2022 Vishal Ltd. purchased a machine for Rs. 8,00,000 and spent Rs. 40,000 on installation and Rs. 20,000 on freight. On 1.10.2023 an additional machine costing Rs. 3,00,000 was bought. On 1.1.2026 the machine purchased on 1.4.2022 became obsolete and was sold for Rs. 4,20,000. Depreciation is charged @ 15% p.a. on the Written Down Value method; accounts are closed on 31st March each year. Prepare the Machinery Account for the years ended 31.3.2023 to 31.3.2026.

(d) (6 marks) Anil and Sunil are partners sharing profits 3:2 with capitals Rs. 6,00,000 and Rs. 4,00,000. The partnership deed provides interest on capital @ 8% p.a., salary to Sunil Rs. 5,000 p.m., and interest on drawings @ 10% p.a. Drawings during the year 2025-26 were Anil Rs. 1,20,000 (evenly at the end of each month) and Sunil Rs. 60,000 (on 1.10.2025). Profit before the above adjustments was Rs. 4,00,000. Prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account and Partners' Capital Accounts (fluctuating).
questions.reasoning: (a) F,F,F,F with reasons; (b) rectify five errors, Suspense agrees at Rs.2,150; (c) WDV machinery a/c, loss on sale computed; (d) appropriations then 3:2 division of residual profit.

questions.text:
(a) (10 marks) From the following Trial Balance of Meera Traders as on 31st March 2026, prepare Trading and Profit & Loss Account for the year and Balance Sheet as at that date:
Debits: Opening Stock 1,20,000; Purchases 7,50,000; Wages 90,000; Carriage Inward 15,000; Salaries 1,10,000; Rent 60,000; Bad Debts 8,000; Debtors 2,40,000; Furniture 1,50,000; Cash & Bank 96,000; Drawings 50,000; Insurance 24,000.
Credits: Capital 5,00,000; Sales 10,80,000; Creditors 1,80,000; Provision for Doubtful Debts 12,000; Discount Received 9,000; Bills Payable 32,000.
Adjustments: (i) Closing stock Rs. 1,60,000 (net realisable value Rs. 1,52,000). (ii) Insurance prepaid Rs. 6,000. (iii) Outstanding wages Rs. 10,000 and salaries Rs. 12,000. (iv) Depreciate furniture @ 10% p.a. (v) Write off further bad debts Rs. 10,000 and maintain provision for doubtful debts @ 5% on debtors. (vi) Goods costing Rs. 20,000 taken by proprietor for personal use, not recorded.

(b) (5 marks) Explain the fundamental accounting assumptions under AS 1 and state the disclosure required when any of them is not followed.

(c) (5 marks) A trader's books show Sales Rs. 12,00,000, Gross Profit ratio 25% on sales, opening stock Rs. 1,50,000 and purchases Rs. 9,20,000. A fire on 31.3.2026 destroyed stock; salvaged stock was Rs. 30,000 and the goods were insured for Rs. 1,00,000 subject to an average clause. Compute the amount of claim.
questions.reasoning: (a) Closing stock at lower of cost/NRV Rs.1,52,000; adjust drawings of goods; provision on Rs.2,30,000. (b) Going concern, consistency, accrual; disclose fact. (c) Loss Rs.1,20,000; claim Rs.80,000 under average clause.

questions.text:
(a) (10 marks) Ravi of Delhi consigned 500 sewing machines costing Rs. 2,000 each to Karan of Kolkata, paying freight and insurance Rs. 30,000. Karan received the consignment and paid octroi Rs. 10,000 and godown rent Rs. 15,000. Karan sold 400 machines at Rs. 2,800 each and is entitled to a commission of 5% on sales plus 2% del credere commission on credit sales. Credit sales amounted to Rs. 4,20,000, of which Rs. 20,000 proved irrecoverable. 20 machines were damaged in transit (normal loss is 5 machines; the balance is abnormal loss). Prepare Consignment Account, Karan's Account and Abnormal Loss Account in the books of Ravi.

(b) (5 marks) X and Y entered into a joint venture to construct a stall, sharing profits 3:2. X contributed Rs. 3,00,000 and Y Rs. 2,00,000 into a joint bank account. Expenses paid from joint bank: materials Rs. 2,80,000, wages Rs. 1,20,000. X supplied his own materials worth Rs. 40,000 and Y paid an architect's fee of Rs. 25,000 personally. Contract price Rs. 6,50,000 was received in the joint bank. Unused materials taken over by Y at Rs. 15,000. Prepare Joint Bank A/c, Joint Venture A/c and Co-venturers' Accounts.

(c) (5 marks) Distinguish between a consignment sale and an outright sale, giving five points of difference.
questions.reasoning: (a) Cost per unit incl. non-recurring exp.; normal loss inflates cost, abnormal loss valued at proportional cost; del credere bears bad debt. (b) JV profit shared 3:2 after taking over materials. (c) Ownership, risk, expenses, returns, account sales.

questions.text:
(a) (10 marks) A, B and C are partners sharing profits in the ratio 5:3:2. Their Balance Sheet as on 31.3.2026 stood as: Liabilities - Capitals: A 4,00,000; B 3,00,000; C 2,00,000; General Reserve 1,00,000; Creditors 1,50,000. Assets - Building 4,50,000; Machinery 2,50,000; Stock 1,80,000; Debtors 2,00,000 less Provision 10,000; Cash 80,000.
C retires on that date on the following terms: (i) Building appreciated by 20% and Machinery depreciated by 10%. (ii) Provision for doubtful debts to be raised to 5% of debtors. (iii) Stock is valued at Rs. 1,70,000. (iv) Goodwill of the firm is valued at Rs. 3,00,000 (no goodwill account is to be raised permanently). (v) C is paid Rs. 1,00,000 immediately and the balance transferred to his loan account. A and B share future profits equally.
Prepare Revaluation Account, Partners' Capital Accounts and the Balance Sheet after retirement.

(b) (5 marks) Explain the accounting treatment of goodwill on admission of a partner when (i) the incoming partner brings goodwill in cash, and (ii) goodwill is not brought in cash. Illustrate the gaining ratio concept.

(c) (5 marks) P and Q are partners with capitals Rs. 5,00,000 and Rs. 3,00,000. They admit R for a 1/4 share; R brings Rs. 3,00,000 as capital. Calculate the value of the firm's goodwill by the capitalisation method and the sacrificing ratio if the new ratio is 3:2:2 and the old ratio was 3:2.
questions.reasoning: (a) Revaluation: +90,000 -25,000 -10,000 -10,000 = +45,000; goodwill adjusted through gaining partners; C's loan balance. (b) Premium method vs adjustment entry. (c) Capitalised value 12,00,000; goodwill 4,00,000; sacrifice computed from 3:2 to 3:2:2.

questions.text:
(a) (10 marks) Sunrise Ltd. issued 1,00,000 equity shares of Rs. 10 each at a premium of Rs. 4 per share, payable: on application Rs. 5 (including premium Rs. 2), on allotment Rs. 6 (including premium Rs. 2) and on first & final call Rs. 3. Applications were received for 1,50,000 shares. Applications for 20,000 shares were rejected and money refunded; the remaining applicants were allotted on a pro-rata basis, excess application money being adjusted against allotment. Mr. Raj, who applied for 6,500 shares, failed to pay the allotment and call money and his shares were forfeited. Of these, 4,000 shares were reissued at Rs. 8 per share fully paid. Pass journal entries and show the Share Capital and Securities Premium balances.

(b) (5 marks) Ganga Ltd. issued 5,000, 12% debentures of Rs. 100 each at a discount of 5%, redeemable at a premium of 10% after 5 years. Pass journal entries for the issue and write a note on the treatment of 'Loss on Issue of Debentures'.

(c) (5 marks) State the conditions under which a company may issue shares at a discount, and briefly explain the accounting for forfeiture and reissue of shares originally issued at a premium where the premium was duly received.
questions.reasoning: (a) Pro-rata 1,30,000:1,00,000; Raj allotted 5,000 shares; compute arrears, forfeiture and capital reserve on reissue. (b) Debit discount+premium payable as Loss on Issue, written off. (c) Sec.53/54 sweat equity; premium received not cancelled.

questions.text:
(a) (8 marks) The Cash Book of Kiran showed a bank overdraft of Rs. 45,000 on 31.3.2026 while the pass book showed a different balance. On scrutiny the following were noted:
(i) Cheques issued for Rs. 68,000 but only Rs. 42,000 presented for payment.
(ii) Cheques deposited Rs. 55,000 of which Rs. 18,000 were credited after 31st March.
(iii) Bank charges Rs. 1,200 and interest on overdraft Rs. 3,500 debited by bank not recorded in cash book.
(iv) A customer directly deposited Rs. 25,000 into the bank.
(v) Insurance premium of Rs. 8,000 paid by bank under standing instructions.
(vi) A cheque of Rs. 12,000 deposited was dishonoured but no entry was made in the cash book.
Prepare a Bank Reconciliation Statement as on 31.3.2026.

(b) (6 marks) Vijay does not maintain complete records. His assets and liabilities were: 1.4.2025 - Stock 80,000; Debtors 1,20,000; Furniture 60,000; Creditors 70,000; Cash 25,000. On 31.3.2026 - Stock 1,10,000; Debtors 1,55,000; Furniture 60,000; Creditors 85,000; Cash 42,000. During the year he introduced additional capital Rs. 50,000 and withdrew Rs. 6,000 per month. Depreciate furniture by 10% and create a provision of 5% on debtors. Compute profit or loss for the year by the statement of affairs method.

(c) (6 marks) On 1.4.2025 a Non-Profit Organisation had subscriptions in arrears Rs. 18,000 and in advance Rs. 12,000. During 2025-26 it received Rs. 3,60,000 as subscriptions, which included Rs. 15,000 for arrears and Rs. 20,000 for the next year. Subscriptions outstanding on 31.3.2026 were Rs. 22,000. Show the Subscription Account and the relevant extracts of the Income & Expenditure Account and Balance Sheet.
questions.reasoning: (a) Start with overdraft per cash book, adjust items to reach pass book balance. (b) Closing capital + drawings 72,000 - additional capital - opening capital = profit after adjustments. (c) Income = 3,60,000 -15,000 -20,000 +12,000 +22,000 = 3,59,000.

questions.text:
(a) A agreed to sell his motorcycle to B for Rs. 60,000. B paid Rs. 5,000 as advance. Before delivery, the motorcycle was destroyed by an accidental fire without any fault of A. B demands refund of Rs. 5,000 and also damages of Rs. 10,000 for loss of bargain. Decide with reference to the doctrine of supervening impossibility and Section 65 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. (5 Marks)
(b) P, a minor, obtained a loan of Rs. 50,000 from Q by falsely representing himself to be a major. Q now sues P for recovery of the loan and, alternatively, seeks to make P liable in tort for deceit. Discuss the legal position of a minor's agreement, the rule of estoppel and the doctrine of restitution. (5 Marks)
(c) X sold his running bakery business along with goodwill to Y and agreed not to carry on a similar business anywhere in India for 10 years. Y later finds X running a bakery in another district after 2 years. Examine the validity of the restraint under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. (5 Marks)
(d) State the essential elements of a valid partnership under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932. Can two partnership firms enter into partnership with each other? (5 Marks)
questions.reasoning: (a) Contract void u/s 56; refund Rs.5,000 u/s 65, no damages. (b) Void ab initio; no estoppel; no restitution of spent money. (c) Valid if reasonable—goodwill sale exception. (d) Agreement, business, profit-sharing, mutual agency; firms cannot be partners, only individuals.

questions.text:
(a) M offers to sell his laptop to N by a letter posted on 1st March. N posts his acceptance on 5th March. On 4th March M posts a revocation letter which reaches N on 6th March, while N's acceptance reaches M on 8th March. Decide whether a contract exists, explaining the rules of communication and revocation of offer and acceptance under Sections 4 and 5 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. (6 Marks)
(b) Distinguish between a contract of indemnity and a contract of guarantee with at least five points of difference. (6 Marks)
(c) 'An agreement without consideration is void, but there are exceptions.' Enumerate and briefly explain the exceptions under Section 25 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. (8 Marks)
questions.reasoning: (a) Contract concluded on 5 March; revocation received after acceptance posted—too late; binding. (b) Parties, liability, purpose, request, recovery rights. (c) Natural love, past voluntary services, time-barred debt, agency, gift, bailment, charitable subscription.

questions.text:
(a) A buyer purchased a second-hand car from a dealer after telling him he needed it for touring purposes. The car proved unfit for touring. Discuss the implied conditions as to quality and fitness under Section 16 of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930 and the buyer's remedies. (6 Marks)
(b) Explain the rules regarding transfer of property in unascertained goods and goods sent on 'sale or return' basis under the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, with examples. (6 Marks)
(c) Who is an 'unpaid seller'? Explain his rights against the goods and against the buyer personally. State whether the right of lien is lost when the seller obtains a decree for the price. (8 Marks)
questions.reasoning: (a) Fitness condition applies—purpose disclosed, reliance on skill; buyer may reject/claim damages. (b) Property passes on unconditional appropriation with assent; sale-or-return on approval/adoption/lapse of time. (c) Lien, stoppage, resale; suit for price/damages; lien not lost by decree.

questions.text:
(a) Explain the doctrine of 'implied authority' of a partner under Section 19 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932. List any five acts which are outside a partner's implied authority. (6 Marks)
(b) R retires from a firm of three partners without giving public notice. Six months later the firm takes a loan from a bank which believed R to be still a partner. Discuss R's liability for acts done after retirement under Section 32. Also state the position of the estate of a deceased partner. (6 Marks)
(c) Distinguish between dissolution of partnership and dissolution of firm. State the grounds on which a court may order dissolution of a firm under Section 44. (8 Marks)
questions.reasoning: (a) Authority to bind firm in usual business; exclusions—arbitration, compromise, immovable property, partner admission, withdraw suit, acquire property. (b) R liable absent public notice; deceased partner's estate not liable. (c) Firm continues vs ends; grounds—insanity, incapacity, misconduct, breach, transfer, loss, just and equitable.

questions.text:
(a) Explain the concept of 'Limited Liability Partnership' and state any six differences between an LLP and a traditional partnership firm under the LLP Act, 2008. (7 Marks)
(b) What is meant by 'designated partner'? State the eligibility conditions and the statutory liabilities of designated partners in an LLP. (6 Marks)
(c) Discuss the doctrine of 'lifting of the corporate veil' under the Companies Act, 2013 with reference to at least four circumstances, judicial or statutory, where the veil may be pierced. (7 Marks)
questions.reasoning: (a) Body corporate, perpetual succession, limited liability, separate legal entity; differences in registration, liability, members, agency. (b) Minimum two, one resident; DPIN; responsible for compliance/penalties. (c) Fraud, tax evasion, enemy character, sham entity, statutory misstatement in prospectus.

questions.text:
(a) Define a 'private company' under the Companies Act, 2013 and state any five privileges available to it as compared to a public company. (6 Marks)
(b) Explain the doctrine of 'indoor management' and its exceptions. How does it differ from the doctrine of constructive notice? (7 Marks)
(c) A public company issued a prospectus containing an untrue statement about the utilisation of issue proceeds. An investor subscribed relying on it and suffered loss. Discuss the civil and criminal liability for misstatement in a prospectus and the defences available to a director. (7 Marks)
questions.reasoning: (a) Restricted transfer, max 200 members, no public invitation; privileges—two members, two directors, fewer meeting formalities. (b) Outsiders presume internal compliance; exceptions—knowledge, suspicion, forgery, negligence; contrast constructive notice. (c) Sections 34/35/36 liability; defences—withdrawal of consent, ignorance, reasonable belief.

questions.text:
Answer all four parts.
(a) (5 marks) State with reasons whether the following are Capital or Revenue in nature: (i) Rs.60,000 paid to remove an old machine and Rs.2,40,000 paid for installing a new imported machine; (ii) Rs.35,000 spent on white-washing the factory building; (iii) Rs.1,20,000 legal fees paid to defend title to land purchased; (iv) Rs.18,000 paid as annual insurance premium on machinery; (v) Rs.90,000 spent on overhauling a second-hand truck purchased, to make it roadworthy.
(b) (5 marks) Rectify the following errors detected after preparation of the Trial Balance, using a Suspense Account: (i) Purchases Book undercast by Rs.5,000; (ii) Goods sold to Ravi Rs.7,400 posted to his account as Rs.4,700; (iii) Rs.2,500 paid for repairs to machinery debited to Machinery A/c; (iv) Discount allowed Rs.600 posted to the credit of Discount Received A/c; (v) Sales returns of Rs.1,800 from Mohan recorded in Purchases Returns Book (party account correctly credited).
(c) (5 marks) On 1.4.2023 a firm had machinery of Rs.8,00,000 (WDV). On 1.10.2023 it purchased a machine for Rs.2,00,000 and on 1.1.2024 sold a machine (original cost Rs.1,50,000 purchased on 1.4.2021) for Rs.90,000. Depreciation is charged @10% p.a. on Written Down Value basis. Prepare Machinery Account for the year ended 31.3.2024.
(d) (5 marks) Distinguish between Provision and Reserve on any five bases, and state how a 'Provision for Doubtful Debts' created in excess of requirement should be treated.
questions.reasoning: (a) Capital: (i),(iii),(v); Revenue: (ii),(iv). (b) Suspense entries; net effect balanced. (c) Sale WDV 1.1.24 = 1,09,350; loss 19,350 approx; closing balance shown. (d) Five distinctions; excess written back to P&L.

questions.text:
(a) (12 marks) From the following Trial Balance of M/s Suraj Traders as on 31st March 2024, prepare Trading and Profit & Loss Account for the year and a Balance Sheet as at that date.
Debits: Opening Stock 1,20,000; Purchases 8,40,000; Wages 1,10,000; Carriage Inward 15,000; Salaries 96,000; Rent 48,000; Bad Debts 6,000; Sundry Debtors 2,40,000; Furniture 1,50,000; Plant & Machinery 4,00,000; Cash & Bank 74,000; Drawings 60,000; Insurance 24,000.
Credits: Capital 6,00,000; Sales 13,80,000; Sundry Creditors 1,80,000; Provision for Doubtful Debts 8,000; Bank Loan @12% (taken 1.7.2023) 2,00,000; Discount Received 15,000.
Adjustments: (i) Closing Stock Rs.1,90,000 (net realisable value Rs.1,84,000); (ii) Depreciate Plant @15% and Furniture @10%; (iii) Provide interest on bank loan; (iv) Insurance includes Rs.6,000 prepaid; (v) Salaries outstanding Rs.8,000; (vi) Write off further bad debts Rs.10,000 and maintain PDD at 5% on debtors.
(b) (8 marks) Explain the accounting treatment of Goods sent on Approval basis and Goods on Consignment lying with the consignee while valuing closing stock. Support with a short illustration.
questions.reasoning: (a) Stock at lower of cost/NRV = 1,84,000; GP and NP computed; Balance Sheet totals agree. (b) Both remain seller's stock at cost + proportionate expenses, not at invoice price.

questions.text:
(a) (10 marks) A, B and C were partners sharing profits 3:2:1. Their Balance Sheet as on 31.3.2024 showed: Capitals A 3,00,000, B 2,00,000, C 1,00,000; General Reserve 60,000; Creditors 1,40,000; Assets: Building 3,00,000, Stock 1,60,000, Debtors 1,20,000 (less PDD 6,000), Cash 2,26,000. C retires on that date. It is agreed that: Building be appreciated by 20%; Stock reduced by 10%; PDD raised to 10% of debtors; Goodwill of the firm valued at Rs.1,80,000 (not to be shown in books); C be paid Rs.60,000 immediately and the balance transferred to his loan account. Prepare Revaluation A/c, Partners' Capital A/cs and the Balance Sheet after retirement.
(b) (10 marks) X and Y are partners sharing 3:2. Z is admitted for 1/5th share bringing Rs.2,00,000 capital and Rs.60,000 as premium for goodwill in cash, retained in business. Compute new profit-sharing ratio and sacrificing ratio, pass journal entries, and explain the treatment if Z had brought only Rs.30,000 towards goodwill.
questions.reasoning: (a) Revaluation profit 60,000-16,000-6,000=38,000 shared 3:2:1; C's dues include reserve and goodwill 30,000; loan balance shown. (b) New ratio 12:8:5; sacrifice 3:2; deficiency debited to Z's capital.

questions.text:
(a) (10 marks) Sunrise Ltd. issued 40,000 equity shares of Rs.10 each at a premium of Rs.4 per share payable: on application Rs.5 (including Rs.2 premium), on allotment Rs.6 (including Rs.2 premium) and on first & final call Rs.3. Applications were received for 60,000 shares. Applications for 8,000 shares were rejected and the balance allotted on pro-rata basis, excess application money being adjusted on allotment. Ramesh, holding 800 shares, failed to pay allotment and call money and his shares were forfeited after the call. 500 of these shares were re-issued at Rs.8 per share fully paid. Pass journal entries and prepare the Share Forfeiture Account.
(b) (10 marks) (i) A company issued 5,000 12% Debentures of Rs.100 each at a discount of 5%, redeemable at a premium of 10% after 5 years. Pass entries for issue. (ii) Explain the provisions relating to issue of shares at a discount and the utilisation of Securities Premium under the Companies Act, 2013.
questions.reasoning: (a) Pro-rata 52,000:40,000; forfeiture credit computed; re-issue discount 1,000 met from forfeiture; balance transferred to Capital Reserve. (b) Loss on issue debited; premium payable credited; Sec.52/53 provisions stated.

questions.text:
(a) (10 marks) Mr. Vijay does not maintain complete books. From the following, prepare Trading & Profit and Loss Account for the year ended 31.3.2024 and Balance Sheet as at that date.
Assets/Liabilities: 1.4.2023 - Stock 90,000; Debtors 1,50,000; Creditors 80,000; Furniture 60,000; Cash & Bank 40,000. 31.3.2024 - Stock 1,10,000; Debtors 1,80,000; Creditors 95,000; Furniture 60,000; Cash & Bank 65,000.
Cash transactions during the year: Received from debtors 6,20,000; Paid to creditors 4,10,000; Cash sales 90,000; Cash purchases 55,000; Expenses paid 1,05,000; Drawings 55,000; Additional capital introduced 40,000.
Additional information: Discount allowed Rs.8,000; Discount received Rs.5,000; Bad debts Rs.12,000; Depreciate furniture @10%; Outstanding expenses Rs.9,000.
(b) (5 marks) Explain the Accounting Standards / concepts relevant to: (i) valuation of inventories, (ii) recognition of revenue from sale of goods, and (iii) the going concern assumption.
(c) (5 marks) State the objectives and advantages of preparing a Trial Balance and explain, with two examples each, errors that a Trial Balance will and will not disclose.
questions.reasoning: (a) Credit sales/purchases derived from debtors & creditors accounts; profit reconciled with capital comparison. (b) AS 2 lower of cost/NRV, AS 9 revenue recognition, going concern. (c) Objectives, errors of principle/compensating not disclosed.
